text.p: Athletic shoe manufacturer Reebok International Ltd announced Tuesday the start of its operations in Venezuela, completing coverage of the Latin American market.

Ruben Semerene, Reebok Operations Manager for Latin America, told Reuters at the end of a news conference that the firm considered the Venezuelan consumer "as one of the most sophisticated in the region."

He said Reebok controlled up to 35 percent of the sports shoe market in the region but had no immediate plans to invest in Venezuela. Reebok said last week it would invest $5 million to build a new plant in Mexico, with operations expected to begin in May 1997.
Reebok executives said the company's absence from Venezuela was mainly due to a long legal dispute with a local firm using a similar brand name which was now solved.
